books.name: Genesis
books.blurb: Creation, the flood, and the patriarchs, ending with Joseph in Egypt.

books.name: Exodus
books.blurb: Israel leaves Egypt, receives the Law at Sinai, and builds the tabernacle.

books.name: Leviticus
books.blurb: Laws for worship, sacrifice, and holy living.

books.name: Numbers
books.blurb: Israel's census and wanderings in the wilderness.

books.name: Deuteronomy
books.blurb: Moses' farewell speeches restating the Law.

books.name: Joshua
books.blurb: Israel enters and settles Canaan.

books.name: Judges
books.blurb: Cycles of failure and rescue before Israel had kings.

books.name: Ruth
books.blurb: A Moabite widow's loyalty and Boaz's kindness.

books.name: 1 Samuel
books.blurb: Samuel, Saul, and the rise of David.

books.name: 2 Samuel
books.blurb: David's reign as king.

books.name: 1 Kings
books.blurb: Solomon's reign and the divided kingdom.

books.name: 2 Kings
books.blurb: The fall of Israel and then Judah.

books.name: 1 Chronicles
books.blurb: Genealogies and David's reign, retold.

books.name: 2 Chronicles
books.blurb: Solomon's temple and the kings of Judah.

books.name: Ezra
books.blurb: Exiles return and rebuild the temple.

books.name: Nehemiah
books.blurb: Rebuilding Jerusalem's walls.

books.name: Esther
books.blurb: A Jewish queen saves her people in Persia.

books.name: Job
books.blurb: A righteous man's suffering and God's answer.

books.name: Psalms
books.blurb: One hundred and fifty songs and prayers.

books.name: Proverbs
books.blurb: Wise sayings for daily life.

books.name: Ecclesiastes
books.blurb: The Preacher's search for meaning.

books.name: Song of Solomon
books.blurb: A poetic celebration of love.

books.name: Isaiah
books.blurb: Judgment and hope, including promises of a coming servant.

books.name: Jeremiah
books.blurb: The weeping prophet warns Judah before exile.

books.name: Lamentations
books.blurb: Poems mourning Jerusalem's fall.

books.name: Ezekiel
books.blurb: Visions of judgment and restoration from exile.

books.name: Daniel
books.blurb: Faithfulness in Babylon and visions of the future.

books.name: Hosea
books.blurb: A prophet's marriage pictures God's faithful love.

books.name: Joel
books.blurb: A locust plague and the day of the LORD.

books.name: Amos
books.blurb: A herdsman calls for justice.

books.name: Obadiah
books.blurb: Judgment on Edom.

books.name: Jonah
books.blurb: A reluctant prophet and the city of Nineveh.

books.name: Micah
books.blurb: Justice, judgment, and a ruler from Bethlehem.

books.name: Nahum
books.blurb: The fall of Nineveh.

books.name: Habakkuk
books.blurb: A prophet questions God and learns to trust.

books.name: Zephaniah
books.blurb: The day of the LORD and a promised remnant.

books.name: Haggai
books.blurb: A call to rebuild the temple.

books.name: Zechariah
books.blurb: Visions encouraging the returned exiles.

books.name: Malachi
books.blurb: The final book of the English Old Testament.

books.name: Matthew
books.blurb: Jesus as Messiah and King, including the Sermon on the Mount.

books.name: Mark
books.blurb: A fast-moving account of Jesus' ministry.

books.name: Luke
books.blurb: Jesus' life told in careful order, with many parables.

books.name: John
books.blurb: Jesus as the Son of God, with the 'I am' sayings.

books.name: Acts
books.blurb: The early church spreads from Jerusalem to Rome.

books.name: Romans
books.blurb: Paul explains the gospel to the church in Rome.

books.name: 1 Corinthians
books.blurb: Paul addresses problems in the Corinthian church.

books.name: 2 Corinthians
books.blurb: Paul defends his ministry and urges generosity.

books.name: Galatians
books.blurb: Freedom in Christ, not the Law.

books.name: Ephesians
books.blurb: The church as Christ's body.

books.name: Philippians
books.blurb: A joyful letter written from prison.

books.name: Colossians
books.blurb: The supremacy of Christ.

books.name: 1 Thessalonians
books.blurb: Encouragement about Christ's return.

books.name: 2 Thessalonians
books.blurb: Further teaching on Christ's return.

books.name: 1 Timothy
books.blurb: Guidance on leading a church.

books.name: 2 Timothy
books.blurb: Paul's final charge to Timothy.

books.name: Titus
books.blurb: Instructions for churches on Crete.

books.name: Philemon
books.blurb: A personal appeal on behalf of Onesimus.

books.name: Hebrews
books.blurb: Jesus as superior to the old covenant.

books.name: James
books.blurb: Faith shown through action.

books.name: 1 Peter
books.blurb: Hope for believers who suffer.

books.name: 2 Peter
books.blurb: A warning against false teachers.

books.name: 1 John
books.blurb: Love, truth, and assurance.

books.name: 2 John
books.blurb: A short letter on truth and love.

books.name: 3 John
books.blurb: A short letter commending hospitality.

books.name: Jude
books.blurb: A short warning to contend for the faith.

books.name: Revelation
books.blurb: John's vision of Christ and the end of the age.

schemes.name: Testament
schemes.question: Which testament?
schemes.tradition: Standard Protestant English Bible: 39 Old Testament books, 27 New Testament books.

schemes.name: Genres
schemes.question: What kind of book?
schemes.tradition: Common English Bible groupings. Acts is placed with History; Revelation with Prophecy.

notes.acts: Acts is a history of the early church.
notes.hebrews: Hebrews reads like a sermon but is grouped with the letters.

schemes.name: Old Testament Sections
schemes.question: Which part of the Old Testament?
schemes.tradition: The usual five-part English arrangement of the 39 Old Testament books.

notes.lamentations: English Bibles place Lamentations with the Major Prophets, after Jeremiah.
notes.daniel: English Bibles place Daniel with the Major Prophets.

schemes.name: Law, Prophets & Writings
schemes.question: Law, Prophets, or Writings?
schemes.tradition: The Hebrew Bible's threefold division, applied to the same 39 books. Luke 24:44 mentions the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms.

notes.joshua: Joshua to Kings are the 'Former Prophets' in the Hebrew Bible.
notes.ruth: English Bibles put Ruth after Judges; the Hebrew Bible places it among the Writings.
notes.daniel: English Bibles put Daniel with the Prophets; the Hebrew Bible places it among the Writings.
notes.lamentations: English Bibles put Lamentations after Jeremiah; the Hebrew Bible places it among the Writings.
notes.esther: In the Hebrew Bible, Esther is among the Writings.
notes.1-chronicles: Chronicles closes the Hebrew Bible, within the Writings.
notes.2-chronicles: Chronicles closes the Hebrew Bible, within the Writings.

schemes.name: New Testament Sections
schemes.question: Which part of the New Testament?
schemes.tradition: The usual five-part English arrangement of the 27 New Testament books.

notes.hebrews: Hebrews is grouped with the General Letters; its author is not named.

schemes.name: Paul or Not?
schemes.question: Did Paul write it?
schemes.tradition: Traditional attribution: thirteen letters name Paul as author. Some scholars question a few of them, and Hebrews does not name its author.

notes.hebrews: Hebrews does not name its author. Some older traditions said Paul, but it is usually listed as unknown.
notes.acts: Acts is by the same author as Luke and features Paul, but it is not a letter by Paul.

schemes.name: Major or Minor?
schemes.question: Major or Minor prophet?
schemes.tradition: 'Major' and 'Minor' refer to the length of the books, not their importance.

notes.lamentations: Lamentations is grouped with the Major Prophets in English Bibles.
notes.daniel: Daniel is grouped with the Major Prophets in English Bibles.

schemes.name: Who Wrote It?
schemes.question: Who wrote it?
schemes.tradition: Traditional attribution: the author named in the book or its title, or the long-standing tradition. 'Unknown' means the text names no author and traditions are divided or tentative. Four books are left out because the tradition is more complicated than one bin can show.

notes.psalms: David wrote many psalms; others, such as Asaph and the sons of Korah, wrote some.
notes.proverbs: Mostly Solomon, with sections from others (Agur, Lemuel, the wise).
notes.ecclesiastes: Traditionally Solomon; the book names 'the Preacher, son of David, king in Jerusalem'.
notes.song-of-solomon: The title attributes the song to Solomon.
notes.genesis: Traditionally Moses, as with the other four books of the Law.
notes.jonah: A prophet named in the title; traditionally he is the author.
notes.daniel: A prophet named in the title; traditionally he is the author.
notes.john: Traditionally the apostle John, as with 1, 2 and 3 John.
notes.revelation: The book names 'John'; tradition identifies him with the apostle.
notes.mark: Traditionally John Mark, a companion of Peter.
notes.luke: Traditionally Luke, a companion of Paul, who also wrote Acts.
notes.acts: Traditionally Luke, who also wrote the Gospel of Luke.
notes.james: Traditionally James, the brother of Jesus.
notes.jude: Jude names himself as the brother of James.
notes.2-peter: Names Simon Peter as author; some scholars question this.
notes.judges: The text names no author. Jewish tradition mentions Samuel.
notes.1-samuel: The text names no author, though the book is named for Samuel.
notes.1-kings: The text names no author. Jewish tradition mentions Jeremiah.
notes.2-kings: The text names no author. Jewish tradition mentions Jeremiah.
notes.1-chronicles: The text names no author. Tradition mentions Ezra.
notes.2-chronicles: The text names no author. Tradition mentions Ezra.
notes.hebrews: The text names no author. Some older traditions said Paul.

excluded.joshua: Tradition says Joshua, but the book records his death; omitted rather than forced into a bin.
excluded.lamentations: Anonymous in the text; tradition links it to Jeremiah. Omitted rather than forced into a bin.
excluded.ezra: Tradition says Ezra, but the book mixes first-person and third-person sections; omitted.
excluded.nehemiah: Opens 'The words of Nehemiah' but is a joined work with Ezra in tradition; omitted.
